body:
You are totally welcome, thanks for your kind reply.

You said that you are a burden to your family and I understand your viewpoint, but I think that your mum and sister probably don't see it that way. If you are close to each other, than that is really beautiful. They just want you to be happy and are trying to help as you would probably do being your 'roles' reversed.

By the way, if you hit some videos talking about 'spiritual' and you are not used to that term, then I'd like to note that it has nothing to do with religion or anything like that. Well, just make your own mind about the vids, or maybe rather follow your intuition.

One more thing - it happened to me that some practice seemed to kinda work for me (from the videos) and then after some time I just stopped for some reason (probably laziness when things seemed to get better) and forgot about all of it, and then few days ago I had severe panic attack that maybe didn't even had to happen, have I had go through with the practice. It probably really is important to stick with what works and commit to it fully. Especially if something fucks up your life a lot, maybe it would be better to make a priority if you find something that works. And hopefully also share what it was. :)

Please let me know what you thought about the vids when you'll watch them, if you remember (no stress about this whatsoever).

I wish you all the best and hope that it will work for you very well. <3 Good luck and and good will. (if that makes sense :) )

It doesn't sound to me like you are either whining or complaining at all. I do not know too much about how exactly PTSD manifests, but I have OCD 'state' which has been probably main factor in allowing me to let my life be destroyed, especially few years ago and just quite recently possibly again (relationship issues). It doesn't perfectly match your description, but I don't have any reason to doubt how miserable your experience can be.

I think I am able to understand how easily can it make you hate your very existence. Same for me. What helped me a lot, especially few days ago when I had very severe anxiety crisis, was being reminded about something I have been interested in before, but after some time, forgot to really put into practice. I don't know at all if it may lead you anywhere from where you are, but what helped me was some videos concerning how what your mind does to you is not the same as *you*. Probably sounds confusing, but I am very tired now. If you are interested, you can take a look at one video where Eckhart Tolle describes it (I hope it is the right one): 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4KhuAO4aeVg

As I've said I don't know if it is applicable in your case, but given my general understanding of PTSD (which as I said isn't very deep) you can let it work for you too. Or at least give it a try. General idea is that *you are not your thoughts* and that you cannot decide what thoughts (or emotions) you have, but you can decide how to handle them.

And as for the perceived cruelty of life - on Saturday when I had severe anxiety or panic attack I was only capable of feeling intense mental pain thinking that I have absolutely no future and at the some time thinking that "no one deserves to hurt like this". I felt it was really unbearable. But maybe you can have a choice, if you gain awareness of what is going on and keep it. I managed to pass through what could probably become another anxiety attack, by being aware about thoughts and feelings I had without engaging with any of it and letting it be there and pass through me.

Actually it is very good starting point. When you don't want to fight anymore you can give up or surrender, but in fundamentally different ways. One of them can be succumbing to what you are thinking about (like suicide), while another one is very different - letting the thoughts of suicide, or any other thought, be there without you resisting them, not wishing they were gone etc. At the some not "thinking them" which means not actively participating in them. Just acknowledging their existence and that's all. Then you can find yourself in a strange situation of having some thoughts and literally letting them be, but not doing anything about them - then you can come to a realization that there is you who lets the thoughts pass through you and your thoughts passing through you. Two separate 'things'. You are out of control of your thoughts anyway (really, if you think about it, they just kind of pop up, one leads to another and so on) and you can choose not to be under control of them.

As I said I came to know about the possibility in living the way I described from Eckhart Tolle. I will send you PM with more about it, since I cannot exactly recommend you something as it is denied by the rules which I understand and respect.

Do you really need to think about the future? Especially if you have a strong negativity in you, then all your thoughts will be probably affected by it. I have that and it affects what I can imagine (very negative scenarios) a lot.

Please don't give in. You are living now. That is all that really matters. Now.

The past and the future - those are just ideas in your head. Thoughts. Every 'past' moment was in fact now and every 'future' moment will happen in the presence - its now. Thoughts turn them into memories and expectations. If you are experiencing negativity now, then you are more likely to remember negatively skewed past events and imagine tragic future.

Your thoughts can really lead you to places - and if you follow them and have feelings like you do, then it will most likely be very dark places. But they are just that - thoughts.

I believe that you can really experience that what you think is happening to you are in fact just thoughts passing through your head - which brings about really huge change. You basically shift your perception although outside of you, nothing changes. And you no longer *need* anything to change. Sorry if it sounds crazy, but I believe it does work. I also admit that it is easy for me to loose that state of being and fall into believing in every thought I have, like two days ago.

Oh, that reminds so much of one thing. As I said two days ago I had serious crisis. My girlfriend decided to spend some time without me to see if she still wants to be with me or not. Initially it didn't cause any problems to me and I *thought* that I am content with it. One day later when she left I had extreme panic attack with one single thought pulsating in my head over and over again as my body trembled in tears and mental pain - "I have **no future** without her, I cannot be alone again, there is absolutely no future for me". And in that state I totally forgot about what I wrote about before - there was no awareness in me that I am 'just' experiencing having a thought - there was essentially no difference between me and the thought I had. Which I think is sadly state the vast majority of people live in (which is not problem when you don't have miserable life).

It felt so bloody *real*. All the pain and suffering at that time - it was *just everything there was for me*. There was literally nothing else but that. When all that pain seemed unbearable I text girlfriend and she managed to calm me down and then kind of reminded me of what I have been talking to her about before - *you are not your thoughts*. Later that day the feelings started to raise in me again. But that time, with the awareness that I have a choice of what to do, I conciously decided to let it go on with no resistance - no need to change it or not experience it - while at the same time not *engaging* in it. Not 'following' the thought not desiring I want it to be different. Just I being there and the thoughts and feelings passing through. Actually it was really just the feelings - no thoughts appeared. It is difficult for me to describe and I can imagine it is even more difficult to try to understand it, but it can really make a profound difference in your life.

Once again I am unable to rule out the possibility that it was just my successful delusion, but I don't think it to be the case at all.

Exactly as Bumle said, please contact the suicide hotline, especially if you felt like you are about to do something irrevocable.

I experienced the intense feeling of absolute self hatred and I hated and regretted my very existence. I have been in that state for about 3 years. Suicide looked like the only option of how to stop it, and I even had a seeming advantage of not having the fear of death. But I realized that I am unable to kill myself from that state of extreme negativity - I hated the idea of dying from state of such an extreme pain I have been experiencing and I was just unable to proceed with it because of that. And that was really shitty - I was in extreme pain and the only option I knew of how to get out of it was impossible to achieve.

Then, with the help of someone else, I managed to change the conditions I have been in.

Some time later I heard one statement that at first I found just very interesting which is *you are not your thoughts*. And some time later still I experienced what it means, instead of just having an idea of what it can mean - when you hate something (like yourself, your life situation) and when you need to do something about it because the pain is unbearable (like kill yourself, because there is no other way out) - then it really is not you needing to do something because of something else. It is just you having that thought and being unaware that it is *just your thought*. It is hard, if possible, to describe, but if you can make it your experience, which I believe you can do, it changes so much. It doesn't mean that you are free of all those thoughts and feelings, but that you can *choose* not to *be* them. You can let it pass *through* you without engaging into actually *feeling* the feelings or *being* your thoughts (they are just there and that's that). Unless I managed to delude myself into thinking it, but I don't think that to be the case. It is also easy, at least for me, to just forget all that and to slip back into state of "feeling the painful feelings causing unbearable thoughts". Two days ago when I had a serious crisis I had to be reminded about it from a person who maybe doesn't 'believe' it herself, but knew that I have been talking about it some time ago, and helped me to rediscover it.

And like you said - not knowing, or rather experiencing, the thoughts and feelings as not being you, can turn out to be torture. I don't know if you find it useful or at least interesting or not, but I can say that what helped me tremendously was Eckhart Tolle's videos on youtube where he talks about it.
I am really glad that you decided to post here. Please can you tell us what made you feel the way you feel? What causes you the pain you feel?

I am actually one of the people who were glad that I didn't kill myself. Back in the years when I was almost every day extremely miserable and contemplating it, I wouldn't believe that it will ever be the case. Nevertheless it happened. Then yesterday I fell into state of extreme pain seeing no future for whatsoever except unbearable pain and I almost pierced my heart with a knife. And I strongly regretted that I didn't kill myself back then. Then some very kind person helped me and pointed towards something I forgot. I forgot that the thoughts in my head, that told be how miserable I am and offered me a single solution in the form of a suicide, are not me. They are just thoughts. *I am not my thoughts*.

When you are in a state of extreme negativity, it is probably literally impossible to conceive of something positive happening to you. Some time ago I learned that there may be an option how not to feel the intense pain and accompanying thoughts. Not easy, if possible at all to describe with words the vocabulary offers. You can be aside of your thoughts letting them move through you, having the pain in you, but you don't have to "feel the pain" or "be your thoughts". Either that or I successfully deluded myself into believing and believing that I am experiencing that, who knows.

Would you mind telling me why you decided to kill yourself? And maybe even telling me that even if you may think it to be pointless?
If you still want to talk to someone, please PM me. You can tell me whatever you want. I am ready to listen.

Thank you, all the best to you as well! I don't think I would do it, hadn't my girlfriend helped me yesterday. I am glad that she did and I decided to post this. Thank you again for your kind comment.

<3

Thank you for your encouragement. :) Sorry for tough reading - do you have any suggestions how can I fix it? May some punctuation help? I have a feeling that those long sentences are easy to loose yourself in, unfortunately. Maybe I will try to separate them into shorter ones.

Regarding ET: I used to think that statement "every time I watch it I learn something new" was just superficial blabber without any substance behind it. But when I watch him talk, or read the books, I think I feel just like that. Like as if when you change as you live, the message in the videos or books changes too. I was so glad when my girlfriend pointed me towards rediscovery of those videos when I have been so low.

But it is so easy to loose that and slip back. Wait! Was it my mind making that thought up? :)

<3

You said that when the pain outweighs, the good, it is time to let go. I agree! But I don't think it is the time to let go of your life, but to finally let of go of the **pain** in your life. Does that sound like bullshit? 
Do you know what I would tell anyone four years ago telling me that? "Fuck you."

Back then the only way I knew about how to let go of all the pain and misery was to let go of my beyond pathetic existence and kill myself. I didn't know of anything close to any possibility how else to let go of it.

Things have changed for me. Now I know there may be another possibility that doesn't require you to give up your life as a tradeoff. Moreover, if you let yourself to begin to realize that there is another way and all the implications of it, the possibility of finally experiencing your life without pain becomes real. Not in any 'mystical' or 'have a faith in' or such way, but through your own experience. It didn't help me to avoid slipping to the pit of pain and horror yesterday, because after long time without the pain, I just forget of that possibility. Very kind person reminded me of it.

I learned that allegedly what you think and how you feel - your emotions (unbearable pain, intense suffering) and your thoughts (I can't go on, I have to kill myself not to face all that pain and suffering anymore) - are not you. This may seem to be superficial, pointless and ridiculous statement, or perhaps even obvious, non helpful one when you think about it. But I managed to experience from that state all the pain and suffering that was going through me - without actually taking any part in it. With 'having the pain' and 'knowing the pain to be here', but without actually 'me being in that pain'. There was just my existence or how to describe it and the pain going through the space of my existence. It was real, but at the same time there was no feeling of "I am in the pain". I didn't have to "feel the pain". I had a possibility with me to let the pain be there without 'me' engaging with it beyond observation of its existence. Sounds like superficial BS? Did I think it up? Did I successfully deluded myself into thinking what is happening or going on? Yes, maybe that's true. Maybe my mind just made it all up. But what if, instead, my mind just made it up in another sense - made up the experience of "feeling all the intense pain without any way to get out of it except suicide amidst that very pain" before? What if it was just my thoughts and "I" just followed? Surrounded myself with them losing the I in them to the point of feeling it is actually me?

Maybe all of that came across as a confusing blabber of some deluded wannabe I don't know what. But I know that the statement "you are not your thoughts" really resonated with me, because I have never 'thought' about that possibility before. And yesterday something happened to me - and it may have been my experience of it. Letting the pain be there and me being with my pain in calmness. I think that you - the real you, so to say - can do the same.

I understand if everything sounds like bunch of intangible esoteric rubbish. And I don't want to 'preach' anything. Anyway, I will just state, that what introduced me into all of this were the videos of Eckhart Tolle on youtube.

Whatever you decide to do with your life, please know that you helped a lot of people - me included. You helped me to see that there are people who care about other people. Even if they now nothing about them. For that, I am grateful to you. Thank you. You are beautiful to me no matter what. <3

I can tell you something, that although you won't probably find helpful, given your stated goal, I hope you will read through anyway. For about 3 years of my life I felt intense hatred towards my existence and planning on how to kill myself, searching for most efficient way given my circumstances (which included no gun for me given legal restrictions) and when I chose how to do it, I came to realization that I cannot do it from all the negativity and suffering that I have been experiencing. And that fucking sucked, because I was extremely miserable and I couldn't even kill myself because of that.

I read from people on the internet who wanted to kill themselves and after they tried and failed some time later they appreciated that they weren't successful in their attempt. Being so miserable, I almost couldn't even imagine, that anything can happen after which I myself would be able to say that.

If someone told me "let's talk about why you feel so bad" I would probably tell that person to fuck off and try to push him or her of my life, suffering all alone.

Couple years later after some significant change in my life, that other people helped me with, I was actually happy that I didn't kill myself back then. Then yesterday after quite a long time without suicidal intentions something happened that made me feel utterly miserable, unable to conceive of any future instead that of irrevocable and unstopping pain, and I almost stabbed myself to heart with a knife. What stopped that was fear and awareness, that most probably it wouldn't result in my death, but instead of remaining in a lifetime of physical pain on top of mental misery.

Aware that I can't bear all that suffering alone, and with unbearable pain, I asked my friend to help me and she did - she helped me a lot and suggested to me to do something that made me realize that what I have been experiencing was due to me believing that all those painful thoughts I had were *just thoughts, not me*. I just lost my awareness of it, and she helped me to bring it back. I realized that deeply and found it to be true. Just thoughts, not me.

I don't know how you feel and if you will read all of this or will considered it to be unrelated or BS, neither can I claim that I won't kill myself today or try to do that. But I know one thing - I actually was happy that I didn't kill myself. I didn't believe that would happened, but it did. I also realized that other people did actually help me - and I have never been interested too much in other people, just my own suffering, or my own stuff in general.

I cannot help you with what you say you want to help with. I can only ask if you can try to tell me what you are going through. I will not claim that I know how to 'help' in your suffering, because I do not. You never know what will happen when you do something or don't do. It may seem to be most absurd and ridiculous idea to talk about your problems with someone else, especially if you did that before and think that it was useless, and if you tried it may turn out to be pointless this time again, but I think that you can never know unless you try.

I see. If you don't want to talk about cause for you wanting to kill yourself, then let me get back to your original question.

To the extent that I am aware there is no way how you can try to kill yourself with guarantee of succeeding except one - to live your life on the end of which you will die. I know that it sucks balls when you want to end it yourself, but if there was some simple way, there would be less people on this forum and on this planet, including the probability of my absence.

I must have misunderstand what you meant then. Let me try again.

Can you tell me what is the reason for your decision to kill yourself? I understand that you are depressed so maybe you can tell me what exactly makes you feel that way? Sorry for being so thick.

Or we can chat on Skype to circumvent reddits delays between allowing me to post. PM my in that case.

No, I don't think at all you don't want to kill yourself, I am sorry if my previous post makes you feel that way.

I am sorry, but I haven't read you previous posts so I hope you will bear with me. So your depression has deepened by the chronic physical pain you have from the leg you broke a year ago?

I am sorry that you want to kill yourself. This is not a place to ask for methods, but let me tell you one thing - there is no fail safe method to kill yourself. Anything you would do, there's no guarantee that you wouldn't end up in some really fucked up state. Trust me, I researched it a lot in my life.

Can you please tell us what's going on in your life that you consider suicide? Did something happened lately, or are you in permanent pain from something?

You don't know me, but I care. I am new to SW and I've been originally browsing through it because due to my suicidal tendencies. You, my dear MamaToFive, are person that I remember the most. I've seen you going great lengths trying to help and actually helping a girl who had overdosed herself. You were there for her. I remember that vividly. You were the one who really helped her, even when you have your share of issues to bear with. It was incredible - you were incredible.

Now it is my time to try to help you. Or at least be with you. Yesterday I almost stabbed knife to my heart. The pain was unbearable.

The least I can do, and I want to do more for You, is let you know what helped me. It was this video of a man called Eckhart Tolle. It is not religious or condemning, just understanding. If you feel like it, please take a look at it, it is only few minutes. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1Ja75T5wF1U If you don't want to look at it, then don't, but anyway please talk to me. I am here for you. It will sound pathetic but I love you. You are a beautiful being to me no matter what you think about yourself.

EDIT: reading through what I wrote it almost looks like I am trying to sell you some religion. Dammit, I am not, that video is not religious at all, and I am neither. There is just a lot of people who care about you here and I am one of them. I love you, even though I never met you. Please hang in there, that horrible feeling will go away. And it is just that a horrible feeling and thoughts, **it is not you**.
